newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end up, technical rebound, low volume.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end up, technical rebound, low volume.

text.p: In largely insipid trade, shares on the Lima stock exchange closed higher on Friday as some local investors found bargains after a week of falling prices, brokers said.
The technical rebound was likely to be short-lived, however, and the market was seen depressed next week due to the economy's slower-than-expected growth, they added.
Friday, the General Index rose 1.54 percent to 1,500.7 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index rose 1.07 percent to 2,090.2 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
Due to rules introduced on the market this week, stocks can continue to be traded, but their prices are fixed one hour before the end of the day's session at 1700 local time (2200 GMT).
At the time prices were fixed Friday there had been 1,311 trades in meager volume estimated at 17.7 million soles ($7.0 million), brokers said.

"The movement in the session was just a question of some people taking up positions, but, because of the low volume, I doubt the gains can be sustained Monday," said Eder Egusquiza of local brokerage Finanval.
The government announced earlier this week that the economy grew 1.9 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared with 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.
Investors now felt Peru was likely to register an annual figure below the government's bottom target of three percent, they added.
Friday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru rose 1.48 percent to 5.50 soles, on a preliminary count of 405,461 million shares.

Among other leaders, tin-miner Minsur rose 1.32 percent to 23.00 soles on a preliminary share count of 32,659, while Banco de Credito rose 1.06 percent to 3.80 soles on a preliminary share total of 98,613.
Backus y Johnston -- the country's largest brewery -- went against the general trend closing down 1.17 percent to 2.54 soles on a preliminary share total of 151,832.
